Convert peak lists into an aligned peak table

Source: R/get_peaktable.R
get_peaktable.Rd

Converts a peak_list object containing peaks from multiple samples into an aligned peak table by clustering peaks across samples according to retention time and (optionally) spectral similarity. The tree is cut at height hmax, whose meaning depends on clust (see hmax).

Usage

get_peaktable(peak_list, ...)

# Default S3 method
get_peaktable(
  peak_list,
  chrom_list,
  response = c("area", "height"),
  use_corrected_rt = NULL,
  hmax = 0.2,
  summarize_by = c("weighted.mean", "median", "mean", "max"),
  plot_it = FALSE,
  ask = plot_it,
  clust = c("rt", "sp.rt"),
  sigma_t = NULL,
  sigma_r = 0.5,
  deepSplit = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...,
  sigma.t = NULL,
  sigma.r = NULL,
  use.cor = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'matched_peak_list'
get_peaktable(
  peak_list,
  pks,
  response = c("area", "height"),
  rt_tol = 0.01,
  na.fill = 0,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'matched_peak_list_set'
get_peaktable(
  peak_list,
  pks,
  response = c("area", "height"),
  rt_tol = 0.01,
  na.fill = 0,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

peak_list

A peak_list object created by get_peaks, or a matched_peak_list created by match_peaks.

...

Additional arguments (currently unused).

chrom_list

A list of chromatographic matrices. Only required when clust = "sp.rt".

response

Peak intensity measure: either "area" (default) or "height".

use_corrected_rt

Logical. Indicates whether to use corrected retention times (rt.cor column) or raw retention times (rt column). Unless otherwise specified, the rt.cor column will be used by default if it exists in the provided peak_list. Either way, they are stored in the rt, start and end rows of pk_meta, and args$use_corrected_rt records which were used.

hmax

Height at which the clustering tree is cut. With clust = "rt", peaks are clustered by complete linkage on retention time, so hmax is the largest retention time difference allowed between any two peaks in the same cluster, in minutes. With clust = "sp.rt", peaks are clustered by average linkage on the dissimilarity \(1 - S_{ij}\), which runs from 0 to 1, and hmax is the maximum tree height passed to cutreeDynamicTree; clusters may be split below it (see deepSplit). There, the default of 0.2 lets peaks with identical spectra sit about 0.67 * sigma_t apart, a third of the mean end - start at the default sigma_t. Ignored for peak lists produced by get_peaks(windows = ) or get_peaks(targets = ), since those peaks are grouped by integration window or target instead of being clustered (see Windows and targets).

summarize_by

How to summarize peak metadata within each cluster. Options are "weighted.mean" (default, weights peaks by their intensity as given by response), "mean", "median" (which aggregate metadata across all peaks in the cluster) or "max" (which selects the most intense peak in the cluster and uses its metadata directly).

plot_it

Logical. If TRUE, for every component a strip plot will be shown indicating the clustering.

ask

Logical. Ask before showing new plot? Defaults to plot_it.

clust

Specify whether to perform hierarchical clustering based on spectral similarity and retention time (sp.rt) or retention time alone (rt). Defaults to rt. Ignored for peak lists produced by get_peaks(windows = ) or get_peaks(targets = ), which are grouped by window or target (see Windows and targets).

sigma_t

Width of Gaussian kernel for retention time similarity, in minutes. Controls the weight given to retention time when clust = "sp.rt". Defaults to half the mean end - start across all peaks.

sigma_r

Width of Gaussian kernel for spectral similarity. Controls the weight given to spectral correlation when clust = "sp.rt". Defaults to 0.5.

deepSplit

Logical. Controls sensitivity to cluster splitting when clust = "sp.rt". If TRUE, returns a larger number of smaller clusters. Defaults to FALSE. For additional information, see cutreeDynamicTree.

verbose

Logical. Whether to warn when two peaks from the same sample fall in the same cluster. Defaults to FALSE.

sigma.t

The sigma.t argument is deprecated. Please use sigma_t, which is in minutes. sigma.t is read in the units of the retention times, as before.

sigma.r

The sigma.r argument is deprecated. Please use sigma_r instead.

use.cor

The use.cor argument is deprecated. Please use use_corrected_rt instead.

pks

A peak_list object from get_peaks. Required when peak_list is a matched_peak_list. Used to retrieve per-peak intensities and metadata.

rt_tol

Numeric. Maximum allowed deviation (in retention-time units) when joining matched peak RTs back to the corresponding row in pks. Defaults to 0.01.

na.fill

Value used to fill cells where no peak was matched in a given sample. Defaults to 0. Only used by the matched_peak_list method.

Value

An S3 peak_table object, containing the following elements:

  • tab: The peak table itself — a data.frame of intensities in a sample × peak configuration. A peak that was not found in a sample, or whose response is negative, is recorded as 0 (na.fill for a matched_peak_list). A peak whose model failed, which get_peaks(targets = ) keeps with a missing height and area, is recorded as NA.

  • pk_meta: A data.frame of peak metadata, one column per peak. Its rows are the wavelength (lambda), the peak number (peak), and whichever of the peak list's rt, start, end, sd, tau, FWHM, r.squared, purity, window_limited and converged columns it has. See the Value section of get_peaks for their meanings. The rows taken from the peak list are summarized across samples according to summarize_by; by default, peaks are weighted by intensity, which reduces the influence of small peaks. With "weighted.mean" or "mean", the converged and window_limited rows become the share of the column's peaks with that flag, so 0.25 means a quarter of them. In a table built from a matched_peak_list, the rows hold the reference sample's values instead.

  • sample_meta: A data.frame of sample metadata: the fields added to the chromatograms with chromConverter::add_metadata() (chromConverter 0.11.0 or later), and any attached with attach_metadata. NA if there are none.

  • instrument_meta: A data.frame of instrumental metadata transferred automatically from the chromatograms.

  • ref_spectra: A matrix of reference spectra (in a wavelength × peak configuration). NA until added with attach_ref_spectra.

  • args: A list of the arguments given to get_peaktable to generate the peak table, with the fit, baseline and max_iter the peaks were fitted with in get_peaks. Its filters element holds any filter_peaks and filter_peaktable calls applied, as code, separated by "; ".

Note

This function is adapted from the getPeakTable function in the alsace package by Ron Wehrens: https://github.com/rwehrens/alsace/blob/master/R/getPeakTable.R.

Clustering

By default, clustering is performed on retention times alone (when clust = "rt"). Alternatively, clustering can also incorporate information about spectral similarity (when clust = "sp.rt") using a similarity function adapted from Broeckling et al., 2014: $$ S_{ij} = \exp\left(-\frac{(t_i - t_j)^2}{2\sigma_t^2}\right) \cdot \exp\left(-\frac{(1 - c_{ij})^2}{2\sigma_r^2}\right) $$ where \(c_{ij}\) is the spectral correlation between spectra \(i\) and \(j\), and \(\sigma_t\) and \(\sigma_r\) control the relative contributions of retention time and spectral similarity, respectively (see sigma_t and sigma_r).

When two peaks from the same sample fall in the same cluster, only the more intense one enters the peak table, with a warning if verbose = TRUE. Such warnings are often benign, but they can also mean hmax is too large. Lowering hmax merges fewer peaks, at the cost of splitting some across multiple clusters; filtering low-intensity peaks before clustering reduces the warnings without that trade-off.

Windows and targets

Peak lists produced by get_peaks(windows = ) are grouped by integration window rather than clustered by retention time, including after correct_peaks. This gives one peak table column per window, ordered by retention time.

Peak lists produced by get_peaks(targets = ) are grouped by target instead of being clustered, each peak going to the matching target. Targets found in no sample are omitted from the peak table. If targets has a name column, the columns are named after the targets.

Peak tables built from get_peaks(windows = ) or get_peaks(targets = ) keep those windows or targets as an attribute of the same name, as a record of how the table was built. The targets attribute lists every target that was searched for, including any found in no sample, which have no column. Neither attribute is updated when columns are removed.

Matched peak lists

match_peaks pairs the peaks in each sample with the peaks of a reference sample, by spectrum as well as retention time. Each column then follows one compound across the samples, even where retention times drift too far for clustering to group the peaks reliably. In crowded stretches of the chromatogram, this works only if neighboring compounds have distinct spectra. This suits targeted analysis (see targeted_analysis) and studies in which one sample, such as a standard mix or a pooled sample, contains every compound of interest.

The peak table has one column for each peak in the reference sample, at each of the specified wavelengths. A peak that's missing in the reference sample gets no column, even if it's present in other samples, so choose the reference with care (see match_peaks).

References

  • Broeckling, C. D., Afsar F.A., Neumann S., Ben-Hur A., and Prenni J.E. 2014. RAMClust: A Novel Feature Clustering Method Enables Spectral-Matching-Based Annotation for Metabolomics Data. Anal. Chem. 86:6812-6817. doi:10.1021/ac501530d .

  • Wehrens, R., Carvalho, E., Fraser, P.D. 2015. Metabolite profiling in LC–DAD using multivariate curve resolution: the alsace package for R. Metabolomics 11:143-154. doi:10.1007/s11306-014-0683-5 .

See also

peak_table, attach_ref_spectra, attach_metadata

Author

Ron Wehrens, Ethan Bass

Examples

data(Sa_pr)
pks <- get_peaks(Sa_pr, lambdas = c('210'))
get_peaktable(pks, response = "area")
